_note: Sums and property received without, or for inadequate, consideration, under other sources (D-201; rulebook OS-GIFT-001). TY 2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 s.92(2)(m): "(i) any sum of money without consideration, the total of which exceeds ₹ 50000, the whole of such sum; (ii) any immovable property— (A) without consideration, the stamp duty value of which exceeds ₹ 50000, the stamp duty value of such property; (B) for a consideration, the stamp duty value of such property that exceeds such consideration, if this excess amount is more than the higher of … (I) ₹ 50000; or (II) 10% of the consideration; (iii) any property, other than immovable property,— (A) without consideration, the aggregate fair market value of which exceeds ₹ 50000, the whole of the aggregate fair market value of such property; (B) for a consideration which is less than the aggregate fair market value of the property by an amount exceeding ₹ 50000, the aggregate fair market value of such property as exceeds such consideration" (p.139); s.92(3)'s exclusions (GiftExclusion). TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.56(2)(x), the same with "fifty thousand rupees" and, since FA 2020 s.29(B)(i) (w.e.f. 1-4-2021), "ten per cent." of the consideration; FA 2021's 20% reaches only s.43CA's 12-11-2020 → 30-6-2021 window, so not this year. Its proviso's exclusions add (XI) a prescribed class and the COVID-19 receipts (XII), (XIII) (FA 2022 s.16), the last limited by OS-GIFT-COVID-DEATH. Values are entered: stamp duty value (s.92(4)(a)), fair market value (S4 r.57). Every regime. Sources: docs/taxplanning-build/sources/2026-10-17-gifts.md.
